directAnswer: To check a web app, you should perform functionality tests, usability assessments, and security checks using various tools and manual methods.
summary: This guide outlines how to effectively check a web app for functionality, usability, and security.

sections.heading: Functionality Testing
sections.body: Ensure all features work as intended. Use automated testing tools like Selenium or manual testing to verify functionalities.

sections.heading: Usability Assessment
sections.body: Evaluate the user experience by conducting user testing sessions and gathering feedback on navigation and interface design.

sections.heading: Security Checks
sections.body: Perform security assessments using tools like OWASP ZAP or Burp Suite to identify vulnerabilities in the web app.

steps.title: Identify Key Features
steps.detail: List all critical features of the web app that need to be tested.

steps.title: Conduct Functionality Tests
steps.detail: Use automated testing tools or manual testing to ensure each feature works correctly across different browsers.

steps.title: Gather User Feedback
steps.detail: Organize user testing sessions to collect feedback on usability and make necessary adjustments.

steps.title: Run Security Tests
steps.detail: Utilize security testing tools to scan for vulnerabilities and address any issues found.

faqs.question: What tools are recommended for functionality testing?
faqs.answer: Selenium, TestCafe, and Cypress are popular choices for automated functionality testing.

faqs.question: How often should I check my web app?
faqs.answer: Regular checks should be performed after major updates and periodically to ensure ongoing functionality and security.

faqs.question: What should I do if I find a security vulnerability?
faqs.answer: Immediately address the vulnerability by patching it and consider informing affected users if necessary.

caveats: Testing methods may vary based on the web app's technology stack.
Manual testing can be time-consuming and may require experienced testers.
